title: Article 88 — Rights of Ministers and Attorney-General as respects Houses

content.overview: Article 88 entitles every Minister and the Attorney-General of India to speak in, and otherwise take part in the proceedings of, either House, any joint sitting, and any committee of Parliament of which he may be named a member, but not to vote unless he is a member of that House.
content.glance: Ministers and AG may speak and take part in either House / joint sitting / committees, but vote only if members of that House.
content.study:
Article 88:
Every Minister and the Attorney-General of India shall have the right to speak in, and otherwise to take part in the proceedings of, either House, any joint sitting of the Houses, and any committee of Parliament of which he may be named a member, but shall not by virtue of this article be entitled to vote.

Examination: speaking/participation rights without automatic voting rights; voting only if the person is a member of the House concerned.

sections.heading: Rights
sections.body: Ministers and Attorney-General: right to speak and take part in either House, joint sittings, and named committees. No vote under this article unless the person is a member of the House.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What rights do Ministers and the Attorney-General have under Article 88?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 88, every Minister and the Attorney-General of India may speak in and otherwise take part in the proceedings of either House, any joint sitting, and any committee of Parliament of which he is named a member, but is not entitled by virtue of this article to vote (voting requires membership of the House).

examTips: Speak/participate yes; vote only if member of the House.

keyTakeaways: Art 88: Ministers/AG may speak in Houses; vote only if members.
